title: Sovereign On-Premise Agentic AI Workbench using Open-Weight Multimodal LLMs for Confidential Industrial Work
dataset_link: Open-source models and publicly available document samples (sample scanned PDFs, sample P&IDs from open datasets) to be used for demonstration; no proprietary data required.
description:
• Background Refineries, PSUs, defence-linked manufacturing units and government offices generate a lot of routine but sensitive knowledge work. Approval notes, board presentations, engineering calculations, code for internal tools, review of scanned drawings and inspection reports. None of this can go through cloud AI assistants like Claude or Codex because the underlying data is confidential: Piping & Instrument Diagrams, financials, vendor negotiations, unreleased designs, internal correspondence, confidential business strategies etc. Company policy keeps this data on premises, so people either do the work manually resulting in productivity gain, or they quietly paste confidential material into public tools anyway. Open weight large reasoning models have reached a point where a genuinely useful assistant built on them is realistic. But nothing deployable exists today that industrial users can actually work with the way they use Claude or Codex.
• Description The idea is a self-hosted, air gapped AI workbench running entirely on the organization's own GPU server. Nothing leaves the premises. The backend should not be locked to one model. It needs to support multiple open weight models at once and automatically pick the right one for a given task based on what that task needs, a coding request handled differently from a document summary request. New open weight models should be addable later without redesigning the system, since this space is moving fast.
The assistant also needs to actually act like an agent. Plan out multi step work, call local tools such as file read and write, code execution in a sandbox, spreadsheet work, internal document search, and iterate on a task instead of answering once and stopping. It needs to handle more than text too: scanned PDFs, handwritten notes, engineering drawings, photographs, read through on device OCR and vision models. Output should be real deliverables, approval notes, PPT/Word/Excel files, working code, calculations with steps shown, not just chat replies. And it needs to ground itself in the organization's own manuals, SOPs and past correspondence through a local knowledge base connector, again with nothing going external.
• Expected Solution A working local deployment, demonstrable on a single workstation or server with a mid range GPU (use a smaller open weight model if 120B class hardware isn't available at the venue), that shows model auto selection across at least two different task types. An agentic task carried through end to end, for example reading a scanned inspection report, pulling out key findings and drafting an approval note as a Word file. A coding task run and verified in a sandbox. A multimodal task involving image or scanned document understanding. The system should also show, through logs or a visible network monitor, that no external calls are made at any point. That's the actual proof of the sovereign claim, not just a statement of it.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on ai applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Sovereign On-Premise Agentic AI Workbench Using Open-Weight Multimodal LLMs

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a self-hosted, air-gapped AI assistant for refinery and defense-linked industrial staff, running entirely on the organization's own servers, so sensitive engineering drawings, financial data, and internal documents never touch a cloud AI service.
overview.why_it_matters: Staff currently either work without AI help or risk pasting confidential data into public tools. A genuinely capable on-premise alternative removes that impossible choice.
pain_points: Sensitive industrial data (P&IDs, financials, unreleased designs) cannot legally or safely go through cloud AI assistants.
Company policy keeps this data on-premises, forcing manual work or risky workarounds.
No deployable, genuinely useful on-premise AI assistant currently exists for this use case.
overview.background: Refineries, PSUs, and defense-linked manufacturing generate sensitive knowledge work that can't use cloud AI tools, but open-weight models have matured enough to make a genuinely useful on-premise alternative realistic, none currently exists in deployable form.
overview.whats_being_asked: A self-hosted, air-gapped AI workbench running on the organization's own GPU server, supporting multiple open-weight multimodal LLMs, for confidential industrial knowledge work.
expected_solution: Air-gapped, self-hosted deployment on organization GPU infrastructure.
Support for multiple open-weight models, not locked to one.
Genuinely usable workflow matching cloud-assistant-quality UX.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Building a genuinely usable, multimodal, model-agnostic on-premise AI workbench is real, substantial systems-engineering work, not a thin wrapper around one model.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires real infrastructure engineering (GPU serving, model orchestration), a genuinely good UX layer, and multimodal document handling (scanned P&IDs, inspection reports) together.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine LLM infrastructure/MLOps expertise, a narrow, technical field distinct from most application-layer PS.

innovation.note: Open-weight model self-hosting is established practice; the value is in genuine usability and multimodal document handling for this specific industrial context.

invention.note: Achievable using existing open-source serving frameworks (vLLM, Ollama, and similar) as a foundation, real effort in the workflow/UX layer.

technical_feasibility.tag: Comfortable, if GPU hardware is available
technical_feasibility.note: Requires access to genuine GPU hardware for meaningful model serving, a real resourcing consideration for a hackathon team.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly enables productivity gains for sensitive industrial work currently blocked by legitimate confidentiality constraints.

architecture.note: Model serving infrastructure, document ingestion, and a usable chat/workbench UI, real but well-understood integration pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with real LLM infrastructure experience and access to GPU hardware. Without genuine GPU access, scope your demo honestly to what's achievable on available hardware, even a smaller open-weight model demonstrated well is more credible than an unworkable claim about a large model.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Extremely well-motivated, concrete real need with genuine organizational stakes (confidentiality compliance versus productivity), not a hypothetical problem.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Without real GPU hardware access, claiming to run genuinely capable open-weight multimodal models would be difficult to substantiate convincingly.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm what GPU hardware access your team actually has (cloud GPU credits, personal hardware, or hackathon-provided infrastructure) and scope your model choice realistically to what you can actually run and demo.

idea_0_4: Confirm your available GPU hardware/compute and choose an open-weight multimodal model that's actually runnable on it.
Design your workbench architecture: model-serving layer, document-ingestion pipeline, and chat/workbench UI.
Split: one person on model serving/infrastructure, one on the document-ingestion and UI layer.
prototype_4_22: Set up your model-serving infrastructure using an established open-source framework.
Build document ingestion for realistic industrial content types (text documents, scanned images).
Start the workbench UI, aiming for genuine usability, not just an API wrapper.
integration_22_30: Connect ingestion, model serving, and UI into one coherent workflow.
Test with realistic sample industrial tasks (summarizing a technical document, reviewing a scanned drawing description).
Confirm the system genuinely runs air-gapped/locally, not silently calling an external API.
polish_30_36: Polish the UI for genuine professional usability, this needs to compete conceptually with cloud AI tool UX.
Rehearse a live demo showing the system handling a realistic confidential-style task entirely locally.
Prepare to discuss your model-agnostic architecture and what scaling to larger models would require.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demo the system running a genuine task entirely offline/air-gapped, disconnect from the internet during the demo if possible, and show it still works, that's the most concrete proof of the sovereignty claim this PS is actually about.

strengths: Extremely well-motivated, concrete real organizational need.
Established open-source serving frameworks provide a credible technical foundation.
weaknesses: Genuine GPU hardware access is a real resourcing constraint for a hackathon team.
Achieving cloud-assistant-quality UX and capability with open-weight models is a real, ongoing technical challenge.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Infrastructure-skill-heavy, this PS's core challenge is genuine model serving and system architecture, not application logic.
team_fit.approach: Confirm GPU access first, this determines your entire model and scope strategy.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The chat/workbench UI scaffolding and standard document-ingestion pipeline.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Real infrastructure decisions about model serving, GPU resource management, and multimodal document handling architecture, that's genuine systems engineering.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A demo that silently calls a cloud API instead of genuinely running on-premise would completely defeat the actual point of this PS, sovereignty and air-gapped operation.

data_resource_availability.status: Open-weight multimodal models are publicly available for download; the constraint is compute/GPU access, not data.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If full GPU access isn't available, demo with a smaller open-weight model that fits available hardware, being honest about the tradeoff versus a full-scale production model.

judge_qna.question: Is this actually running locally/air-gapped, or calling an external API?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Demonstrate this directly, ideally by disconnecting from the internet during the demo and showing the system still functions, that's the concrete proof of the sovereignty claim.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would production-scale GPU infrastructure for this actually require?

judge_qna.question: How does an open-weight model's capability compare to what cloud assistants like Claude or Codex currently offer?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about the capability gap for your chosen model size, and describe the specific use cases (routine document review, code review) where an open-weight model is genuinely sufficient versus where it would fall short.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your roadmap for closing that capability gap as open-weight models improve?
